key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
engineering_relevance: The planar architecture offers a route to more efficient, environmentally stable hybrid silicon photovoltaics without substrate texturing.
method: Benchmark trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si references on untextured substrates.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and impermeable protective barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 ambient days, compared with approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75 days of ambient aging; longer-term durability and scalable fabrication remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
